In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel signaling pathways and their molecular components that regulate mitochondrial activity and function in cancer cells.
the study of the mechanisms that control mitochondrial activity in the context of cancer cells and their exploitation for the development of novel therapeutic approaches to fight cancer.
the study of the role of compartmentalization of signaling pathways and proteolysis in the regulation of mitochondria in different types of cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mitochondria are the key elements of the metabolic network that support cancer cell growth and survival and that the signaling networks controlling mitochondrial activity are potential targets for the treatment of human cancer.

the cAMP· PKA pathway is a master regulator of mitochondria and that the compartmentalization of PKAs at mitochondria by AKAPs is essential for the fine tuning and the control of mitochondrial functions.

the compartmentalization of signaling pathways at mitochondria is essential to regulate their activities in the control of energy production and metabolism, and in the modulation of cell growth and survival, thus contributing to the development of cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

mitochondria are not simply a source of energy for the cells, but they are also a hub for the integration of multiple signals and pathways that control cell metabolism and survival in response to environmental cues.
mitochondria are the central hub for the integration of signaling networks and metabolic processes that regulate cancer cell survival, proliferation and metastasis.
the compartmentalized signaling network at mitochondria, acting through PKA and AKAPs, controls important aspects of mitochondrial activity, including biogenesis, respiration, and metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
compartmentalization of cAMP-dependent PKA signaling at mitochondrial level, mediated by AKAPs, is a key element in the fine-tuning of mitochondrial activity in cancer cells.
the control of mitochondrial function is essential for the survival of cancer cells.

mitochondria are not only a target but they can also be a source of signaling pathways, and their functional interference with mitochondrial activities can have a profound impact on cell survival and proliferation.
